text_note.zh: 这里用的是通行本《唐诗三百首》的文字。原始文字里的“鼇”“麤”是旧写法，现在写作“鳌”“粗”。“䝙”是一种猛兽的名字，规范字就写作“䝙”。
text_note.en: This is the text in the common editions of Three Hundred Tang Poems. Two characters, áo ("giant sea turtle") and cū ("coarse"), appear in the source in old forms and are written in today's standard forms here. The rare character chū, the name of a fierce beast, is kept as it is.

readings.zh: 接受朝拜，读 cháo，不读 zhāo。
readings.en: Meaning to receive the homage of visitors, read cháo, not zhāo.

readings.zh: 表示“年”，读 zǎi，不读 zài。
readings.en: Meaning "years", read zǎi, not zài.

readings.zh: 一种像老虎的猛兽，读 chū。
readings.en: The name of a tiger-like beast, read chū.
A kind of big bear, read pí.
Meaning long, read cháng.
Meaning a chief minister, read xiàng, not xiāng.
Meaning a chief minister, read xiàng.

readings.zh: 人名裴度，读 dù，不读 duó。
readings.en: The name Pei Du, read dù, not duó.
Xiàng yìn is a chief minister's seal, read xiàng.
Cǎn dàn means gloomy, read dàn.
The name Li Su, read sù.
Meaning to carry along, read zài, not zǎi.

readings.zh: 计算、估量，读 zī。“不訾”就是数不清。
readings.en: Meaning to count or measure, read zī. Bù zī means beyond counting.
The name Pei Du, read dù.

readings.zh: 写作、作为，读 wéi，不读 wèi。
readings.en: Meaning to write, to make, read wéi, not wèi.

readings.zh: “稽首”是跪下磕头的大礼，稽读 qǐ，不读 jī。
readings.en: In qǐ shǒu, a deep bow with the head to the ground, it is read qǐ, not jī.
Meaning to do, read wéi, not wèi.

readings.zh: 关联、取决于，读 xì，不读 jì。
readings.en: Meaning to depend on, read xì, not jì.

readings.zh: 铺开、摆开，读 pū，不读 pù。
readings.en: Meaning to spread out, read pū, not pù.

readings.zh: 量米的斗，读 dǒu，不读 dòu。
readings.en: Meaning a grain measure, read dǒu, not dòu.
Meaning a sentence, read jù.
Meaning few, read shǎo, not shào.

readings.zh: 拉、拖，现在读 zhuài；古代也读 yè，同“曳”。
readings.en: Meaning to drag, read zhuài today. In old times it was also read yè, like the word for "to tow".
Meaning a chief minister, read xiàng.
Meaning one time through, read guò.

readings.zh: 同“又”，读 yòu。“七十有二”就是七十二。
readings.en: Here it means "and", read yòu. Qī shí yòu èr is simply seventy-two.

readings.zh: “封禅”是古代帝王祭天地的大典，禅读 shàn，不读 chán。
readings.en: In fēng shàn, the grand rite to Heaven and Earth, it is read shàn, not chán.

glosses.zh: 元和天子：唐宪宗。元和是他的年号（806—820）。
glosses.en: yuán hé tiān zǐ: Emperor Xianzong of Tang. Yuanhe (806–820) was the name of his reign.

glosses.zh: 神武姿：像神一样英明勇武的样子。
glosses.en: shén wǔ zī: a look as wise and brave as a god.

glosses.zh: 彼何人哉：他们是什么样的人呢？意思是宪宗可以和他们相比。
glosses.en: bǐ hé rén zāi: what kind of men were they? Meaning Xianzong could stand beside them.

glosses.zh: 轩与羲：轩辕（黄帝）和伏羲，传说中上古的圣明帝王。
glosses.en: xuān yǔ xī: Xuanyuan (the Yellow Emperor) and Fuxi, wise rulers of legend.

glosses.zh: 上雪列圣耻：洗刷前面几代皇帝留下的耻辱。雪，洗掉。列圣，历代先帝。
glosses.en: shàng xuě liè shèng chǐ: to wipe away the shame left by the emperors before him. Xuě, "snow", here means to wash clean.

glosses.zh: 法宫：皇帝处理朝政的正殿。
glosses.en: fǎ gōng: the main hall where the emperor ran the government.

glosses.zh: 朝四夷：让四方各族都来朝拜。
glosses.en: cháo sì yí: to have peoples from every side come and bow to him.

glosses.zh: 淮西：唐代的淮西镇，在今天河南东南部一带，那里的军阀长期不听朝廷的命令。
glosses.en: huái xī: the Huaixi region, in today's southeast Henan. Its warlords refused the court's orders for many years.

glosses.zh: 有贼五十载：叛贼占据了五十年左右。
glosses.en: yǒu zéi wǔ shí zǎi: rebels had held it for about fifty years.

glosses.zh: 封狼生䝙䝙生罴：大狼生出䝙，䝙又生出罴。封狼，大狼。䝙、罴，都是猛兽。比喻淮西的叛将一代接一代，越来越凶。
glosses.en: fēng láng shēng chū chū shēng pí: the great wolf gave birth to a chu, and the chu to a bear. Chu and pí are fierce beasts. It means the rebel leaders followed one after another, each fiercer than the last.

glosses.zh: 不据山河据平地：不是靠着高山大河的险要，而是在平原上占地称霸。
glosses.en: bù jù shān hé jù píng dì: they did not hold mountains and rivers for defense, but took over the open plain.

glosses.zh: 长戈利矛：长长的戈，锋利的矛，都是古代兵器。
glosses.en: cháng gē lì máo: long dagger-axes and sharp spears, old weapons.

glosses.zh: 日可麾：传说古时有人打仗时挥动戈，让快落山的太阳退了回来。这里说叛军很狂妄，以为什么都能做到。麾，挥。
glosses.en: rì kě huī: in an old story, a warrior waved his dagger-axe and the setting sun moved back. Here it means the rebels were so proud they thought they could do anything. Huī means to wave.

glosses.zh: 圣相：贤明的宰相。
glosses.en: shèng xiàng: a wise chief minister.

glosses.zh: 相曰度：这个宰相名叫裴度。
glosses.en: xiàng yuē dù: the minister was named Pei Du.

glosses.zh: 贼斫不死：元和十年，刺客刺杀宰相武元衡，裴度也被砍伤，却没有死。斫，砍。
glosses.en: zéi zhuó bù sǐ: in 815 assassins killed the chief minister Wu Yuanheng. Pei Du was also cut, but he did not die. Zhuó means to cut with a blade.

glosses.zh: 神扶持：好像有神在保佑他。
glosses.en: shén fú chí: as if a god were protecting him.

glosses.zh: 腰悬相印：腰上挂着宰相的大印。
glosses.en: yāo xuán xiàng yìn: with the chief minister's seal hanging at his waist.

glosses.zh: 都统：统率各路军队的总指挥。
glosses.en: dū tǒng: commander-in-chief over all the armies.

glosses.zh: 阴风惨澹：冷风吹着，天色阴沉。
glosses.en: yīn fēng cǎn dàn: a cold wind under a gloomy sky.

glosses.zh: 天王旗：皇帝军队的大旗。
glosses.en: tiān wáng qí: the banner of the emperor's army.

glosses.zh: 愬武古通：四位将领：李愬、韩公武、李道古、李文通。
glosses.en: sù wǔ gǔ tōng: four generals: Li Su, Han Gongwu, Li Daogu and Li Wentong.

glosses.zh: 牙爪：爪牙，就是得力的武将。这里是夸奖的话，说他们勇猛能干。
glosses.en: yá zhǎo: teeth and claws, that is, strong fighting officers. Here it is praise.

glosses.zh: 仪曹外郎：礼部员外郎，一种官名，这里指李宗闵。
glosses.en: yí cáo wài láng: an official in the Ministry of Rites, here Li Zongmin.

glosses.zh: 载笔随：带着笔跟随军队，负责写文书。
glosses.en: zài bǐ suí: going along with the army, brush in hand, to write its papers.

glosses.zh: 行军司马：军中的高级参谋官，这里指韩愈。
glosses.en: xíng jūn sī mǎ: a senior staff officer of the army, here Han Yu.

glosses.zh: 虎貔：老虎和貔，都是猛兽，比喻勇猛的士兵。
glosses.en: hǔ pí: tigers and pí, fierce beasts, standing for brave soldiers.

glosses.zh: 入蔡缚贼：攻进蔡州城，把叛军首领吴元济绑了起来。蔡，蔡州，淮西的中心城市。
glosses.en: rù cài fù zéi: breaking into Caizhou and tying up the rebel leader Wu Yuanji. Caizhou was the main city of Huaixi.

glosses.zh: 献太庙：把俘虏献到太庙。太庙，皇帝祭祀祖先的地方。
glosses.en: xiàn tài miào: presenting the captive at the Great Temple, where the emperor honored his ancestors.

glosses.zh: 功无与让：功劳大，没有人比得上，用不着推让。
glosses.en: gōng wú yǔ ràng: the deed was so great no one could match it, so there was no one to yield to.

glosses.zh: 恩不訾：皇帝给的赏赐多得数不清。訾，计算。
glosses.en: ēn bù zī: the emperor's rewards were beyond counting. Zī means to count.

glosses.zh: 汝度：你裴度。汝，你。
glosses.en: rǔ dù: you, Pei Du. Rǔ means "you".

glosses.zh: 从事愈：你的部下韩愈。从事，下属官员。
glosses.en: cóng shì yù: Han Yu, your officer. Cóng shì means a staff officer under someone.

glosses.zh: 宜为辞：应该来写碑文。辞，文章，这里指碑文。
glosses.en: yí wéi cí: should write the words. Cí here means the text for the stele.

glosses.zh: 拜稽首：跪下磕头行大礼。
glosses.en: bài qǐ shǒu: kneeling and bowing with the head to the ground.

glosses.zh: 蹈且舞：又跳又舞，古代臣子向皇帝表示感谢和高兴的一种礼节。
glosses.en: dǎo qiě wǔ: stepping and dancing, an old way for an official to show thanks and joy before the emperor.

glosses.zh: 金石刻画：刻在铜器、石碑上的文字。
glosses.en: jīn shí kè huà: writing carved on bronze and stone.

glosses.zh: 大手笔：写重要文章的大作家。
glosses.en: dà shǒu bǐ: a great writer trusted with the most important texts.

glosses.zh: 不系于职司：不看他担任什么职务。系，关系。职司，职务。
glosses.en: bù xì yú zhí sī: does not depend on what post he holds.

glosses.zh: 当仁自古有不让：遇到该做的事，自古以来就不推让。出自《论语》“当仁，不让于师”。
glosses.en: dāng rén zì gǔ yǒu bù ràng: when it is right to act, one has never stepped aside. It comes from the Analects: "When it comes to doing good, do not yield even to your teacher."

glosses.zh: 言讫：说完。讫，完毕。
glosses.en: yán qì: having finished speaking.

glosses.zh: 屡颔天子颐：皇帝一次次点头。颔，点头。颐，下巴。
glosses.en: lǚ hàn tiān zǐ yí: the emperor nodded again and again. Hàn means to nod; yí is the chin.

glosses.zh: 公：指韩愈，是尊称。
glosses.en: gōng: Han Yu, a polite way to name him.

glosses.zh: 斋戒：洗澡、换衣、不喝酒吃肉，让身心干净，表示郑重。
glosses.en: zhāi jiè: bathing, changing clothes, and giving up wine and meat to make body and mind clean, to show respect.

glosses.zh: 濡染大笔：把大笔蘸饱墨汁。濡，沾湿。
glosses.en: rú rǎn dà bǐ: soaking a big brush in ink. Rú means to wet.

glosses.zh: 何淋漓：多么痛快、饱满啊！淋漓，墨汁饱满，也比喻写得酣畅。
glosses.en: hé lín lí: how rich and flowing! Lín lí means dripping with ink, and also writing freely and boldly.

glosses.zh: 点窜：修改字句。
glosses.en: diǎn cuàn: to touch up and change words.

glosses.zh: 尧典、舜典：《尚书》里的两篇，记尧、舜的事，是最古老庄重的文章。
glosses.en: yáo diǎn, shùn diǎn: two chapters of the Book of Documents about the ancient rulers Yao and Shun, among the oldest and most solemn writings.

glosses.zh: 清庙、生民：《诗经》里的两篇，用来歌颂祖先和功德。两句说韩愈学习、化用了最古老的经典文章。
glosses.en: qīng miào, shēng mín: two poems in the Book of Songs that praise ancestors and their deeds. The two lines mean Han Yu learned from and reshaped the oldest classics.

glosses.zh: 破体：打破常规的写法，指韩愈的碑文不按当时流行的格式写。一说指书法上的字体。
glosses.en: pò tǐ: a style that breaks the usual rules, meaning Han Yu did not follow the fashion of the day. Another view says it refers to the style of the handwriting.

glosses.zh: 丹墀：宫殿前涂成红色的台阶，代指朝廷。
glosses.en: dān chí: the red-painted steps before the palace hall, standing for the court.

glosses.zh: 表：臣子给皇帝的一种奏章。
glosses.en: biǎo: a formal letter from an official to the emperor.

glosses.zh: 昧死上：冒着死罪呈上。这是古代给皇帝上书时表示恭敬的套话。
glosses.en: mèi sǐ shàng: "I present this at the risk of death", a set phrase of respect used when writing to the emperor.

glosses.zh: 咏神圣功：歌颂皇帝的伟大功业。神圣，指皇帝。
glosses.en: yǒng shén shèng gōng: praising the emperor's great deeds. Shén shèng here means the emperor.

glosses.zh: 三丈：约十米。丈，长度单位。
glosses.en: sān zhàng: about ten meters. Zhàng is an old unit of length.

glosses.zh: 字如斗：每个字有斗那么大。斗，量米的器具。
glosses.en: zì rú dǒu: each character as big as a grain bucket. Dǒu is a measure for rice.

glosses.zh: 负以灵鳌：碑下面用石刻的神龟驮着。鳌，传说中的大海龟。
glosses.en: fù yǐ líng áo: carried on the back of a stone turtle. Áo is a giant turtle of legend.

glosses.zh: 蟠以螭：碑顶刻着盘绕的螭。螭，传说中没有角的龙。
glosses.en: pán yǐ chī: with chi coiled on top. Chī is a hornless dragon of legend.

glosses.zh: 句奇语重：句子奇特，用语庄重。
glosses.en: jù qí yǔ zhòng: sentences that are unusual, words that are weighty.

glosses.zh: 喻者少：能看懂的人很少。喻，明白。
glosses.en: yù zhě shǎo: few people understood it. Yù means to understand.

glosses.zh: 谗之天子：在皇帝面前说坏话。谗，说别人坏话。
glosses.en: chán zhī tiān zǐ: speaking ill of it to the emperor. Chán means to slander.

glosses.zh: 言其私：说碑文偏心，不公平。私，偏私。
glosses.en: yán qí sī: saying it was unfair, playing favorites. Sī here means bias.

glosses.zh: 拽碑倒：把碑拉倒。拽，拉。
glosses.en: zhuài bēi dǎo: dragging the stele down. Zhuài means to pull.

glosses.zh: 相磨治：把碑上的字磨掉。治，处理。
glosses.en: xiāng mó zhì: grinding the words off the stone.

glosses.zh: 斯文：这篇文章。斯，这。
glosses.en: sī wén: this piece of writing. Sī means "this".

glosses.zh: 元气：天地间最根本的气，万物都靠它生长。
glosses.en: yuán qì: the first, basic energy of heaven and earth, which everything grows from.

glosses.zh: 先时：在碑被磨掉之前。
glosses.en: xiān shí: before the stele was ground down.

glosses.zh: 入人肝脾：深深地印在人们心里。肝脾，代指内心。
glosses.en: rù rén gān pí: entered people's livers and spleens, that is, sank deep into their hearts.

glosses.zh: 汤盘：商汤洗澡用的盘，上面刻着“苟日新，日日新，又日新”。
glosses.en: tāng pán: the washbasin of King Tang of Shang, carved with "If you can renew yourself one day, renew yourself every day".

glosses.zh: 孔鼎：孔子祖先正考父的鼎，上面刻着铭文。
glosses.en: kǒng dǐng: the bronze cauldron of Zheng Kaofu, an ancestor of Confucius, carved with words.

glosses.zh: 述作：刻在上面的文字。
glosses.en: shù zuò: writings, here the words carved on them.

glosses.zh: 今无其器存其辞：现在那些器物都没有了，可上面的文字还流传着。
glosses.en: jīn wú qí qì cún qí cí: the objects are gone now, but their words live on.

glosses.zh: 呜呼：唉，感叹声。
glosses.en: wū hū: oh, alas, a cry of strong feeling.

glosses.zh: 圣皇：圣明的皇帝，指唐宪宗。
glosses.en: shèng huáng: the wise emperor, Xianzong.

glosses.zh: 相与：一起。
glosses.en: xiāng yǔ: together.

glosses.zh: 烜赫：声名显赫，非常光彩。
glosses.en: xuǎn hè: shining, glorious.

glosses.zh: 流淳熙：留下美好、光明的影响。淳，纯厚。熙，光明。
glosses.en: liú chún xī: leaving behind a pure and bright influence.

glosses.zh: 不示后：不能给后人看到。
glosses.en: bù shì hòu: is not shown to later people.

glosses.zh: 曷：怎么。
glosses.en: hé: how.

glosses.zh: 三五：三皇五帝，传说中上古的圣明君主。
glosses.en: sān wǔ: the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, wise rulers of legend.

glosses.zh: 相攀追：赶上、和他们并列。
glosses.en: xiāng pān zhuī: to catch up with them and stand beside them.

glosses.zh: 愿书万本：希望把它抄写一万份。
glosses.en: yuàn shū wàn běn: I wish to copy it ten thousand times.

glosses.zh: 诵万过：读一万遍。过，遍。
glosses.en: sòng wàn guò: to read it aloud ten thousand times. Guò means "times".

glosses.zh: 口角流沫：读得嘴角都起了白沫。
glosses.en: kǒu jiǎo liú mò: reading until foam comes from the corners of my mouth.

glosses.zh: 右手胝：抄得右手都磨出了老茧。胝，老茧。
glosses.en: yòu shǒu zhī: copying until my right hand grows calluses. Zhī is a callus.

glosses.zh: 七十有二代：七十二代。传说古代到泰山祭天地的帝王有七十二位，这里指很多很多代。
glosses.en: qī shí yòu èr dài: seventy-two generations. Legend says seventy-two ancient rulers went to Mount Tai for the grand rites. Here it means generation after generation.

glosses.zh: 封禅：帝王到泰山祭天祭地的隆重大典，只有功业最大的帝王才能举行。
glosses.en: fēng shàn: the grand rite at Mount Tai to Heaven and Earth, held only by rulers with the greatest deeds.

glosses.zh: 玉检：封禅时用来封存文书的玉片。
glosses.en: yù jiǎn: jade covers used to seal the writings offered at the grand rite.

glosses.zh: 明堂基：明堂的基石。明堂，帝王举行最隆重典礼的地方。
glosses.en: míng táng jī: the foundation stone of the Bright Hall, where emperors held their grandest ceremonies.

translation.zh: 元和年间的皇帝英明勇武，像神一样，
translation.en: The Yuanhe emperor was wise and brave, like a god.

translation.zh: 古代的黄帝和伏羲又是什么人呢？他完全可以和他们相比。
translation.en: Who were the Yellow Emperor and Fuxi? He could stand beside them.

translation.zh: 他发誓要洗刷前面几代皇帝留下的耻辱，
translation.en: He swore to wipe away the shame of the emperors before him,

translation.zh: 坐在正殿里，让四方各族都来朝拜。
translation.en: and to sit in his main hall as peoples from every side came to bow.

translation.zh: 淮西被叛贼占据了五十年，
translation.en: For fifty years rebels had held Huaixi,

translation.zh: 像大狼生䝙、䝙又生罴，一代比一代凶。
translation.en: like a wolf that bore a chu, and a chu that bore a bear, each fiercer than the last.

translation.zh: 他们不靠山河险要，就在平原上称霸，
translation.en: They held no mountains or rivers, just ruled the open plain,

translation.zh: 拿着长戈利矛，狂妄得以为能把太阳挥回去。
translation.en: and with long spears and sharp blades, thought they could wave the sun back.

translation.zh: 皇帝得到了一位贤明的宰相，名叫裴度，
translation.en: The emperor found a wise chief minister, named Pei Du.

translation.zh: 刺客砍他却没砍死，好像有神保佑。
translation.en: Assassins cut him but he did not die, as if a god protected him.

translation.zh: 他腰挂宰相大印，当上了总指挥，
translation.en: With the minister's seal at his waist, he became commander-in-chief,

translation.zh: 冷风阴沉，皇家的大旗迎风飘扬。
translation.en: and the emperor's banners flew in a cold, gloomy wind.

translation.zh: 李愬、韩公武、李道古、李文通是他得力的武将，
translation.en: Li Su, Han Gongwu, Li Daogu and Li Wentong were his fighting arms,

translation.zh: 礼部员外郎带着笔跟在军中。
translation.en: and an official of the Ministry of Rites came along with brush in hand.

translation.zh: 行军司马又聪明又勇敢，
translation.en: The army's senior staff officer was clever and brave,

translation.zh: 十四万大军像老虎和貔一样勇猛。
translation.en: and the hundred and forty thousand soldiers were fierce as tigers.

translation.zh: 他们攻进蔡州，捉住叛贼，献到太庙，
translation.en: They broke into Caizhou, tied up the rebel and presented him at the Great Temple.

translation.zh: 功劳大得没人比得上，皇帝的赏赐数也数不清。
translation.en: No deed could match theirs, and the emperor's rewards were beyond counting.

translation.zh: 皇帝说：“裴度，你的功劳第一，
translation.en: The emperor said, "Pei Du, yours is the first deed,

translation.zh: 你的部下韩愈应该来写碑文。”
translation.en: so your officer Han Yu should write the words."

translation.zh: 韩愈跪下磕头，又跳又舞地谢恩，说：
translation.en: Han Yu knelt, bowed to the ground, and danced his thanks, saying:

translation.zh: “刻在铜器石碑上的文章，我能写。
translation.en: "Writing to be carved on bronze and stone: this I can do.

translation.zh: 自古以来，人们都说要请大手笔来写，
translation.en: Since ancient times, people have called on the great writers,

translation.zh: 这件事不看担任什么官职。
translation.en: and the task does not depend on one's post.

translation.zh: 遇到该做的事，自古就不推让。”
translation.en: When a thing is right to do, one has never stepped aside."

translation.zh: 他说完，皇帝连连点头。
translation.en: When he finished, the emperor nodded again and again.

translation.zh: 韩公回家后斋戒，坐在小屋里，
translation.en: Han Yu went home, made himself clean, and sat in his small room,

translation.zh: 把大笔蘸饱墨汁，写得多么酣畅！
translation.en: soaked his big brush in ink, and how freely it flowed!

translation.zh: 他化用了《尚书》里《尧典》《舜典》的字句，
translation.en: He reshaped words from the chapters on Yao and Shun in the Book of Documents,

translation.zh: 改写了《诗经》里《清庙》《生民》的诗篇。
translation.en: and reworked the poems "Pure Temple" and "Birth of the People" from the Book of Songs.

translation.zh: 文章写成，打破常规，写在纸上，
translation.en: When the piece was done, in a style that broke the rules, he wrote it out on paper,

translation.zh: 清早再次下拜，把它摆在宫殿的红台阶前。
translation.en: and early in the morning bowed again and laid it out on the red palace steps.

translation.zh: 奏章上写着：“臣韩愈冒死呈上，
translation.en: His letter said, "Your servant Han Yu presents this at the risk of death:

translation.zh: 歌颂圣上的伟大功业，请刻在碑上。”
translation.en: words praising Your Majesty's great deeds, to be carved on a stele."

translation.zh: 石碑高三丈，字有斗那么大，
translation.en: The stele was three zhang tall, each character as big as a grain bucket,

translation.zh: 下面有神龟驮着，上面盘着螭龙。
translation.en: carried on a sacred turtle and topped with coiled dragons.

translation.zh: 可是文章句子奇特、用词庄重，懂的人很少，
translation.en: But its sentences were unusual and its words weighty, and few understood them.

translation.zh: 有人在皇帝面前说坏话，说碑文偏心。
translation.en: Someone slandered it to the emperor, saying it played favorites.

translation.zh: 于是用百尺长的绳子把碑拉倒，
translation.en: So with a rope a hundred feet long they dragged the stele down,

translation.zh: 用粗砂大石把上面的字磨掉。
translation.en: and ground off its words with coarse sand and big stones.

translation.zh: 可是韩公的文章像天地元气一样，
translation.en: Yet Han Yu's writing was like the first energy of heaven and earth:

translation.zh: 早在这之前就深深印在人们心里了。
translation.en: long before, it had already sunk deep into people's hearts.

translation.zh: 商汤的浴盘、孔家的铜鼎都刻过文字，
translation.en: King Tang's washbasin and the Kong family's cauldron once bore carved words;

translation.zh: 现在器物没了，文字还在流传。
translation.en: the objects are gone today, but the words remain.

translation.zh: 唉，圣明的皇帝和贤明的宰相，
translation.en: Ah, the wise emperor and the wise minister:

translation.zh: 一起建立了辉煌的功业，留下美好的影响。
translation.en: together they won great glory and left a bright, pure legacy.

translation.zh: 如果韩公的文章不能给后人看到，
translation.en: If Han Yu's writing is not shown to those who come later,

translation.zh: 他们怎么能和三皇五帝并列呢？
translation.en: how can they stand beside the ancient sage kings?

translation.zh: 我愿意把它抄一万份，读一万遍，
translation.en: I wish to copy it ten thousand times and read it ten thousand times,

translation.zh: 读得嘴角冒沫，抄得右手长茧。
translation.en: until my mouth foams and my right hand grows calluses.

translation.zh: 让它传上七十二代，
translation.en: Let it be handed down for seventy-two generations,

translation.zh: 成为封禅大典的玉检和明堂的基石。
translation.en: to be the jade seal of the grand rites and the foundation stone of the Bright Hall.

background.zh: 唐宪宗元和十二年（817年），宰相裴度亲自督战，将军李愬雪夜攻进蔡州，捉住了叛将吴元济，平定了淮西。韩愈当时是裴度的行军司马，奉命写了《平淮西碑》。碑文把功劳主要归给裴度，李愬的妻子是公主的女儿，她向皇帝哭诉说碑文不公平。宪宗就下令把碑拉倒、磨掉字，改让段文昌重写。几十年后，李商隐写了这首诗，为韩愈的碑文鸣不平。具体写作时间不能确定。
background.en: In 817, under Emperor Xianzong, the chief minister Pei Du went to the front himself. General Li Su attacked Caizhou on a snowy night and captured the rebel leader Wu Yuanji, ending the Huaixi revolt. Han Yu was Pei Du's senior staff officer and was ordered to write the Stele on Pacifying Huaixi. The text gave most of the credit to Pei Du. Li Su's wife, the daughter of a princess, complained to the emperor that it was unfair. Xianzong had the stele pulled down and its words ground away, and ordered Duan Wenchang to write a new one. Decades later Li Shangyin wrote this poem to speak up for Han Yu's text. The exact year it was written is not known.

author_note.zh: 李商隐（约813—约858），字义山，号玉谿生，晚唐著名诗人。他最出名的是写得含蓄、朦胧的爱情诗和《无题》诗。这首《韩碑》却写得直接有力，用了很多古奥的字句，有意学习韩愈的文风，可以看出他对韩愈非常敬佩。
author_note.en: Li Shangyin (about 813 to about 858), also called Yishan, was a famous poet of the late Tang. He is best known for subtle, dreamlike love poems and his "Untitled" poems. This poem is different. It is direct and forceful, full of old, difficult words, and deliberately copies Han Yu's style. It shows how much he admired Han Yu.

appreciation.zh: 这首诗像在讲一个完整的故事，可以分成三段。第一段写打仗：皇帝英明，淮西叛贼凶狠，裴度带着猛将和十四万大军攻进蔡州，大获全胜。第二段写写碑：皇帝点名让韩愈写，韩愈又跳又舞地接下任务，回家斋戒，用大笔一挥而就，碑高三丈，字大如斗，气派极了。第三段写碑的命运：有人说坏话，碑被拉倒、字被磨掉。可诗人说，好文章像天地间的元气，早就进了人们心里，就像古代铜器没了，上面的话还在。最后他说愿意抄一万遍、读一万遍，读到嘴冒沫、手起茧，让它传下去。诗写得又硬又重，就像一块石碑，读起来能感到诗人心里的不平和敬佩。
appreciation.en: This poem tells a whole story in three parts. Part one is the war. The emperor is wise, the Huaixi rebels are fierce, and Pei Du leads strong generals and 140,000 soldiers into Caizhou to win. Part two is the writing of the stele. The emperor names Han Yu, who accepts with a dance of thanks, goes home, cleanses himself, and writes it in one bold sweep. The stele is three zhang tall with characters as big as buckets. It is grand. Part three is the stele's fate. Someone slanders it, and it is pulled down and ground blank. But the poet says great writing is like the first energy of heaven and earth: it is already in people's hearts. Old bronzes are lost, yet their words remain. At the end he says he will copy it and read it ten thousand times, until his mouth foams and his hand is callused, so it can be handed down. The poem is hard and heavy, like a stone stele itself, and you can feel the poet's anger at the injustice and his deep respect for Han Yu.
